title: Solos credited to Buck Clayton that were really his
summary: Edison names solos he took on Basie records, such as Every Tub, Sent for You Yesterday and Easy Does It, and Dance offers to correct the listings.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Oh. Well, of course, everybody thinks it's Buck that played pretty all the time.
Well, yeah, that was me. I took a lot of solos, you know, that Buck got the credit for. Like "Every Tub", "Sent for You Yesterday."
Now, "Sent for You Yesterday" is not exactly a wild solo but it's a kind of fierce solo, you know. I always thought that was quite a -- when I heard that, I can
still remember the first time. That was something different then.

Yeah. Then "Easy Does It," that's my solo on there. A lot of people thought it was Buck. Oh, a lot of solos that I played in the Basie band Buck got credit for because -- well, he was due the credit, you know. He'd been in the band and he had a name for himself and I was just a beginner mostly, you know. People hadn't heard about me. They still thought -- well, it's neither here nor there now, you know. We both came out --
Well, it should be put right because --
"Easy Does It," that was my solo. "Taxi War Dance."
I've got a book that Huques Pana-ssie did where all the solos / list , and I'll send you a copy of that and you can check that.
Because that should be corrected. There's no call to --
Yeah. Well, I played the solo on "Panassie Stomp" and oh, well, I made "Louisiana", that was my solo; "Shorty George."
Well, once you arrived, then, you were proceeding to take about half the trumpet solos?
Yeah, yeah. I did quite a bit of it,

you know. But Buck was the favorite, you know. It didn't make any difference to me who took the solo. That's one thing about Basie's band, it didn't matter who played the solo, just so you got to play, you know. And if you didn't swing, you wouldn't have a solo, anyway. They'd take it away from you and give it to somebody else. Pres would ring a bell that he used to have, if it wasn't swing he'd ring this bell, you know. That was the cue that that wasn't the solo for you; give it to somebody else.
